Rett syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder that primarily affects females. Diagnosis is made on the basis of clinical features and requires regression of neurological development that is followed by a recovery or stabilization phase. The causative gene encodes methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2), which binds methylated DNA and regulates gene transcription.
